text:
Florida got the result its play warranted, and it took a third-period wrister from Matthew Tkachuk to make that official. His goal at 11:20, set up by Sam Bennett, broke a 1-1 tie and held up as the winner, 2-1 over Los Angeles at Crypto.com Arena. The Panthers deserved to win in 62 percent of simulated replays of every shot, and the chances behind that number were not close to even over the full night.

Alex Laferriere gave the Kings a lead with 1:00 left in the first, a wrist shot Erik Haula helped create that carried just an 8 percent chance of scoring. It was the kind of goal a team gets when the period has been even (Florida 0.52 expected goals, Los Angeles 0.49). The second period tilted hard the other way. Florida generated 1.48 expected goals to 0.95 and tied it at 3:49 when Seth Jones scored on a wrister, assisted by Lars Eller. For the game, the Panthers attempted 65 shots to the Kings' 47 and finished with 2.69 expected goals against 2.02.

Neither power play cashed in, with Florida going 0 for 6 and Los Angeles 0 for 5, so the game was settled at even strength, where Florida also held the edge, 1.24 to 0.88. Jacob Markstrom stopped 29 of 30 shots and saved about one goal more than expected. Darcy Kuemper faced 20 and allowed two, about 0.7 goals better than the quality of shots suggested. The Kings stayed in it on goaltending and one good chance. It wasn't enough against a team that kept the puck and the better looks.
